<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" id=PARA4473.2><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3200><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I><B>We rely on the services of our executive officers, whose knowledge of our business and industry would be extremely difficult to replace.</B></I></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3201><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3202><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our success depends to a significant degree upon the continuing contributions of our management.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management may voluntarily terminate their employment with us at any time upon short notice.&nbsp;&nbsp;The loss of key personnel could harm our business. Failure to retain key personnel could harm our ability to carry out our business strategy and compete with other companies.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3203><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3204><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;<B>Risks Related to Our Strategy to Increase Value for Stockholders</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3205><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3206><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I><B>Since the closing of the tender offer on November 10, 2010, the Company has fewer resources and alternatives to pursue its strategy to enhance stockholder value.</B></I></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3207><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3208><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On November 10, 2010, the Company completed a tender offer to acquire up to 13,846,153 shares of its common stock at a cash price of $3.25 per share, or a total price of $45 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;A total of 13,214,401 shares were properly tendered and not withdrawn in the offer and was purchased by the Company at a total price of $42,946,803.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of January 31, 2014, the Company had cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $10.9 million, net of broker payable of $1.4 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;This amount will be used, along with revenues and receivables, to fund the Company&#8217;s future operating expenses, as well as to pursue its strategy to enhance stockholder value.&nbsp;&nbsp;With a reduced cash balance, the Company has fewer resources to explore various alternatives to enhance value for stockholders, and a more limited range of available alternatives.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3209><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3210><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I><B>A significant portion of our working capital could be expended in pursuing strategies that do not enhance value for stockholders.</B></I></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3211><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3212><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We expect that the investigation of each specific opportunity, structuring of any related transaction, drafting and execution of relevant agreements, disclosure documents and other instruments will require substantial time and attention and substantial costs including, but not limited to, due diligence costs for accountants, attorneys and other advisors/consultants.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, we may investigate developing a new business, which may include substantial legal and/or financial advisory costs, or to make downpayments or pay exclusivity or similar fees in connection with structuring and negotiating business combinations.&nbsp;&nbsp;If we determine not to, or are unable to consummate a specific opportunity, the costs incurred will not be recoverable.&nbsp;&nbsp;Any such event will result in a loss to us of the related costs incurred, which could materially and adversely affect our subsequent attempts to locate and combine with another business.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3213><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3214><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I><B>Our current corporate strategy depends in part on our ability to successfully establish a new venture, acquire an existing company or make another investment.&nbsp;&nbsp; Our failure to execute this strategy could reduce our earnings and reduce our cash reserves.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, our investments, new ventures and/or acquisitions may be subject to substantial risk.</B></I></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3215><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3216><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our current corporate strategy involves exploring various alternatives to enhance stockholder value through establishing&nbsp;a new venture or&nbsp;acquiring an existing business, as well as through other investment opportunities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Potential risks related to this strategy include lack of necessary capital, the inability to satisfy closing conditions, failure to identify suitable or economically acceptable alternatives, and the inability to successfully integrate a new business into our operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our ability to enhance value to stockholders and manage growth depends upon our ability to continue to invest in operational, financial and management information systems and to attract, retain, motivate and effectively manage our employees.&nbsp;&nbsp;The inability to effectively manage the integration of new operations could reduce our focus on subsequent acquisitions and current operations, which, in turn, could negatively impact our earnings and growth.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, even if we develop a new business or invest in or acquire another company, there is no guarantee that such transactions will be successful in producing revenue or profits.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3217><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3218><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I><B>We are pursuing a strategy which may not enhance value for stockholders.</B></I></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3219><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3220><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Since the completion of the KMC Transaction in April 2008, we have been exploring various alternatives to enhance stockholder value through establishing&nbsp;a new venture or&nbsp;acquiring an existing business, as well as through other investment opportunities. However, we may not be able to identify an appropriate alternative.&nbsp;&nbsp;If we do identify a suitable opportunity for a new business, acquisition or investment, we may not be able to successfully and satisfactorily execute the opportunity.&nbsp;&nbsp;Furthermore, if we are successful in executing the opportunity, the integration of the opportunity will involve a number of risks and presents financial, managerial and operational challenges.&nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore, we cannot assure that this strategy will enhance value for our stockholders.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3221><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3222><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I><B>We could experience losses on our investments in marketable securities.</B></I></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3223><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3224><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As part of our interim investment activities, we invest in marketable securities from time to time.&nbsp;&nbsp;At January 31, 2014 and 2013 we held marketable securities with a market value of approximately $4.3 million and $2.9 million respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;In fiscal 2014, we had $2.2 million in net realized losses (as discussed above in <I><B>Interim Investment Activities</B></I> section) and $0.5 million decrease in net unrealized losses, compared to $0.1 million in net realized gains and $2.0 million increase in net unrealized losses in fiscal 2013. Unrealized gains or losses are expressed on a net after tax basis and are included in the total comprehensive income. Such investments are subject to various general market and investment-specific risks, and there is no assurance that in future periods the Company will not experience losses on its current or future investments.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3225><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3227><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3228><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Although we are&nbsp;not currently engaged in the business of investing, reinvesting, or trading in securities, and do not currently hold ourselves out as being engaged in those activities,&nbsp;Peerless may be deemed to be an &#8220;inadvertent investment company&#8221; under section 3(a)(1)(C) of the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended (the &#8220;Investment Company Act&#8221;), if the value of its investment securities (as defined in the Investment Company Act) is found to be more than 40% of its total assets (exclusive of government securities and cash and certain cash equivalents).</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3229><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>

In the event that Peerless were to be required to register as an investment company under the Investment Company Act, Peerless would be forced to comply with substantive requirements under the Act, including:</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3333><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3334><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B>&nbsp;Item&nbsp;7.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3335><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3336><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following analysis contains forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties.&nbsp;&nbsp;The statements contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K that are not purely historical are forward-looking statements within the meaning of Section&nbsp;27A of the Securities Act and Section&nbsp;21E of the Exchange Act, including without limitation, statements regarding our expectations, beliefs, intentions or strategies regarding the future.&nbsp;&nbsp;All forward-looking statements included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K are based on current expectations, estimates, forecasts and projections about the industry in which we operate, management&#8217;s beliefs and assumptions made by management.&nbsp;&nbsp;These statements are not guarantees of future performance and involve certain known and unknown risks, uncertainties and assumptions that are difficult to predict.&nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore, actual outcomes and results may differ materially from what is expressed or forecasted in such forward-looking statements.&nbsp;&nbsp;We undertake no obligation to update publicly any forward-looking statements, whether as a result of new information, future events or otherwise.&nbsp;&nbsp;For a discussion of factors and trends that could impact our business and results, please refer to the section above entitled &#8220;Risk Factors.&#8221;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3337><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3338><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following should be read in conjunction with the audited consolidated financial statements and related notes thereto contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3339><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3340><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B>Highlights</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3341><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B>&nbsp;</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3342><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B></B>Our revenues increased 45% from $2.5 million in fiscal 2013 to $3.6 million in fiscal 2014, primarily attributable to two customers who had exhausted their block licenses and are currently paying us on a pay-as-you-go basis.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3343><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3344><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B>Critical Accounting Policies</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3345><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3346><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#8220;Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations&#8221; addresses our consolidated financial statements, which have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States.&nbsp;&nbsp;The preparation of these consolidated financial statements requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and the disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the consolidated financial statements and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period.&nbsp;&nbsp;On an ongoing basis, management evaluates its estimates and judgments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management bases its estimates and judgments on historical experience and on various other factors that they believe are reasonable under the circumstances, the results of which form the basis for making judgments about the carrying values of assets and liabilities that are not readily apparent from other sources.&nbsp;&nbsp;Actual results may differ from these estimates under different assumptions or conditions.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3347><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3348><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management believes the following critical accounting policies, among others, affect its more significant judgments and estimates used in the preparation of its consolidated financial statements.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3349><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3350><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Revenue Recognition</I></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3351><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3352><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We account for our software revenues in accordance with provisions of Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) Accounting Standards Codification &#8482;&nbsp;(&#8220;ASC&#8221;) 985-605,<I> Software &#8211; Revenue Recognition</I> and ASC 605-25,<I> Revenue Recognition &#8211; Multiple-Element Arrangements</I> (formerly known as Statement of Position, or SOP, 97-2, &#8220;Software Revenue Recognition&#8221;, as amended by SOP 98-9, Staff Accounting Bulletin No.104, &#8220;Revenue Recognition&#8221;, and Emerging Issues Task Force 99-19, &#8220;Reporting Revenue Gross as a Principal versus Net as an Agent&#8221;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Over the past several years, we entered into block license agreements that represent unit licenses for products that will be licensed over a period of time.&nbsp;&nbsp;In accordance with ASC 985-605 and 605-25, revenue is recognized when the following attributes have been met: 1) an agreement exists between us and the OEM selling product utilizing our intellectual property and/or a third party&#8217;s intellectual property for which we are an authorized licensor; 2) delivery and acceptance of the intellectual property has occurred; 3) the fees associated with the sale are fixed and determinable; and 4) collection of the fees are probable.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under our accounting policies, fees are fixed and determinable if 90% or more of the fees are to be collected within a twelve-month period.&nbsp;&nbsp;If more than 10% of the payments of fees extend beyond a twelve-month period, such fees are recognized as revenues when they are due for payment.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3353><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3354><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For fees on multiple element arrangements, values are allocated among the elements based on vendor specific objective evidence of fair value (&#8220;VSOE&#8221;).&nbsp;&nbsp;We generally establish VSOE based upon the price charged when the same elements are sold separately.&nbsp;&nbsp;When VSOE exists for all undelivered elements, but not for the delivered elements, revenue is recognized using the &#8220;residual method&#8221; as prescribed by ASC 605-25.&nbsp;&nbsp;If VSOE does not exist for the undelivered elements, all revenue for the arrangement is deferred until the earlier of the point at which such VSOE does exist for the undelivered elements or all elements of the arrangement have been delivered, unless the only undelivered element is a service in which revenue from the delivered element is recognized over the service period.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3355><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" id=PARA6392.1><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<DIV style="WIDTH: 100%; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" id=PGBK6392 >
<DIV style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%" id=PGFTR6392 >&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" id=PGNUM6392 >11</DIV>
<HR style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%; HEIGHT: 2px; COLOR: #000000" noShade>

<DIV style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; WIDTH: 100%" id=PGHDR6392 >&nbsp;</DIV></DIV>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" id=PARA6392.2><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3356><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Product Licensing Cost</I></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3357><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3358><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We provide an accrual for estimated product licensing costs owed to third party vendors whose technology is included in the products sold by us.&nbsp;&nbsp;The accrual is impacted by estimates of the mix of products shipped under certain of our block license agreements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The estimates are based on historical data and available information as provided by our customers concerning projected shipments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Should actual shipments under these agreements vary from these estimates, adjustments to the estimated accruals for product licensing costs may be required.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such adjustments have historically been within management&#8217;s expectations.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3359><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3360><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Certain product licensing revenues are dependent, in part, on the timing and accuracy of product sales reports received from our OEM customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;These reports are provided only on a calendar quarter basis and, in any event, are subject to delay and potential revision by the OEM.&nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore, we are required to estimate all of the recurring product licensing revenues for the last month of each fiscal quarter and to further estimate all of our quarterly revenues from an OEM when the report from such OEM is not received in a timely manner.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the event we are unable to estimate such revenues accurately prior to reporting financial results, we may be required to adjust revenues in subsequent periods.&nbsp;&nbsp;Actual results have historically been consistent with management&#8217;s estimates.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3361><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3362><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Allowance for Doubtful Accounts</I></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3363><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3364><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We grant credit terms in the normal course of business to our customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;We continuously monitor collections and payments from our customers and maintain allowances for doubtful accounts for estimated losses resulting from the inability of any customers to make required payments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Estimated losses are based primarily on specifically identified customer collection issues.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the financial condition of any of our customers, or the economy as a whole, were to deteriorate, resulting in an impairment of their ability to make payments, additional allowances might be required.&nbsp;&nbsp;Actual results have historically been consistent with management&#8217;s estimates.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3365><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3366><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Stock-based Compensation</I></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3367><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3368><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On February&nbsp;1, 2006 the Company adopted FASB ASC 718,<I> Compensation &#8211; Stock Compensation</I> (formerly known as FAS 123(R)<I> Share-Based Payments</I>) using the modified-prospective transition method. Compensation cost recognized subsequent to adoption includes: (i)&nbsp;compensation cost for all share-based payments granted prior to, but unvested as of January&nbsp;31, 2006, based on the grant date fair value, which is determined using a Black-Scholes option pricing model and (ii)&nbsp;compensation cost for all share-based payments granted subsequent to February&nbsp;1, 2006, based on the grant-date fair value using a Black-Scholes option pricing model to estimate the grant date fair value of share-based awards.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3369><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3370><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We use our actual stock trading history over a five year period as a basis to calculate the expected volatility assumption to value stock options. The expected dividend yield is based on Peerless&#8217; practice of not paying dividends.&nbsp;&nbsp;The risk-free rate of return is based on the yield of U.S. Treasury Strips with terms approximating or equal to the expected term of the option.&nbsp;&nbsp;The expected life in years is based on historical actual stock option exercise experience.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3371><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3372><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ASC 718 requires forfeitures to be estimated at the time of grant and revised, if necessary, in subsequent periods if actual forfeitures differ from those estimates.&nbsp;&nbsp;If actual forfeitures vary from our estimates, we will recognize the difference in compensation cost in the period the actual forfeitures occur.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3373><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3374><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Compensation expense for share-based awards is recognized using a straight-line, or single-option method.&nbsp;&nbsp;We recognize these compensation costs over the service period of the award, which is generally the options vesting term of three to four years.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3375><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 50.6pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3376><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We recorded approximately $961,000 in share-based compensation expense for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;We granted 6,000 options and 258,088 shares of restricted common stock during the fiscal year ended January 31, 2014. As discussed in &#8220;Note 3. Stock-Based Compensation Plans&#8221; in the notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements, in connection with the new employment agreement entered into on July 11, 2013 with Mr. Timothy Brog, the Company&#8217;s Chairman and Chief Executive Officer (the &#8220;Employment Agreement&#8221;), Mr. Brog agreed to forfeit 150,000 shares of restricted common stock that remained unvested under the previous employment agreement between the Company and Mr. Brog dated August 26, 2010 (the &#8220;2010 Agreement&#8221;). As part of the Employment Agreement, the Company granted 250,000 shares of restricted common stock to Mr. Brog. Although the fair value of the newly granted restricted common stock would be amortized as stock-based compensation, there would be no offset from the fair value previously expensed, relating to the 150,000 shares that were forfeited, due to the fact that the requisite service period had been satisfied.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3377><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" id=PARA6393.1><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" id=PARA6393.2><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3378><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Income taxes</I></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3379><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3380><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Deferred income taxes are recognized for the tax consequences in future years resulting from differences between the tax bases of assets and liabilities and their financial reporting amounts at each year-end based on enacted tax laws and statutory rates applicable to the periods in which the differences are expected to reverse.&nbsp;&nbsp;Valuation allowances are established, when necessary, to reduce deferred income tax assets to the amount expected to be realized.&nbsp;&nbsp;Income tax provision is the tax payable for the period and the change during the period in net deferred income tax assets and liabilities.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3381><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3382><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In February 2007, the Company adopted FASB ASC 740-10,<I> Income Taxes</I> (formerly known as FIN 48 Accounting for Uncertainty in Income Taxes an Interpretation of FAS109).&nbsp;&nbsp;See &#8220;Note 5. Income Taxes&#8221; in the notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements for further information.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3383><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3384><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ASC 740-10 clarifies the accounting and reporting for uncertainties in income tax law.&nbsp;&nbsp;This interpretation prescribes a comprehensive model for the financial statement recognition, measurement, presentation and disclosure of uncertain tax positions taken or expected to be taken in income tax returns.&nbsp;&nbsp;The interpretation requires that the tax effects of a position be recognized only if it is &#8220;more-likely-than not&#8221; to be sustained by the taxing authority as of the reporting date.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the tax position is not considered &#8220;more-likely-than not&#8221; to be sustained, then no benefits of the position are to be recognized.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3385><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3386><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In assessing whether deferred tax assets can be realized, we consider whether it is more likely than not that some portion or all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized.&nbsp;&nbsp;The ultimate realization of deferred tax assets depends upon the generation of future taxable income or reversal of deferred tax liabilities during the periods in which those temporary differences become deductible.&nbsp;&nbsp;We consider the scheduled reversal of deferred tax liabilities, projected future taxable income, and tax planning strategies in making this assessment.&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3387><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 39.6pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3388><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As previously reported in our Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 31, 2012, we reversed $1,376,000 of tax liabilities, consisting of $1,265,000 in an unrecognized tax benefit and approximately $111,000 in related accrued interest expense.&nbsp;&nbsp;This reversal of tax liabilities related to an unrecognized tax benefit from the Company&#8217;s tax position taken for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2009, in connection with the completion of the three year statute of limitations period applicable to the corresponding tax return.&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3389><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3390><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of January&nbsp;31, 2014, we had net deferred tax assets of approximately $134,000 which consisted primarily of the net tax effect on unrealized losses on marketable securities classified in Other Comprehensive Income.&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3391><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3392><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B>Results of Operations</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3393><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3394><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;<I>Net Income</I></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3395><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3396><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Net loss for the year ended January&nbsp;31, 2014 was $0.9 million&nbsp;or $0.32 per basic and diluted share, compared to a net income of $1.8&nbsp;million, or $0.56 per basic and $0.53 per diluted share in fiscal year 2013. Higher non-cash stock-based compensation expense, as discussed above, as well as realized losses in marketable security were the primary reasons for the net loss incurred in fiscal 2014, while the reversal of tax liabilities in fiscal 2013 accounts for most of the net income during that period. Excluding the effect of the tax liabilities reversal discussed above, net income for the year ended January&nbsp;31, 2013 was $0.4&nbsp;million or $0.12 per basic and diluted share.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3397><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3398><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Revenues for fiscal year 2014 were $3.6 million, compared to $2.5&nbsp;million in fiscal year 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;This 45% increase&nbsp;in revenue was primarily attributable to two customers who had exhausted their block licenses and are currently paying us on a pay-as-you-go basis.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3399><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3400><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Cost of Revenues</I></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3401><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3402><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;Product licensing costs were $0.3&nbsp;million in fiscal year 2014 compared to $0.2&nbsp;million in fiscal year 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;In fiscal 2014, we made adjustments to reduce such costs by approximately $0.1 million. Without the effect of these adjustments, product licensing costs would have been $0.4 million. The increase in product licensing cost in fiscal year 2014 was the result of higher licensing revenues on which we were obligated to pay a third party for licensing its technology in fiscal year 2014. &nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3403><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3404><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;<I>Gross Margin</I></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3405><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3406><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Gross margin as a percentage of total revenues was 92% in fiscal year 2014 compared to 91% in fiscal year 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;The higher gross margin in fiscal 2014 was the result of lower fees being paid to third parties due to a change in the product mix generating licensing revenues.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3407><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3410><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Operating expenses for fiscal year 2014 were $2.1 million compared to $1.6 million for fiscal year 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp; This increase was primarily attributable to the $0.8 million non-cash stock-based compensation expense (&#8220;Non-Cash Stock Expense&#8221;), related to the restricted stock award granted to our Chairman and Chief Executive Officer in connection with his new employment agreement, as previously reported in the Form 10Q for the three month period ended July 31, 2013. Excluding all stock-based compensation expenses, operating expenses would have been $1.2 million for fiscal 2014, compared to $1.3 million for fiscal 2013. This decrease in operating expenses was primarily attributable to our continued cost reduction effort, in several areas including legal fees, reduction in personnel and the outsourcing of certain functions.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3411><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>

Commitments&#8221; in the notes to the Consolidated&nbsp;Financial Statements for further information. </FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3422><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B>Liquidity and Capital Resources</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3423><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3424><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of January 31, 2014, our cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities (net of broker payable of $1.4 million included in other current liabilities) totaled $10.9 million, a decrease of $0.9 million from $11.8 million at January 31, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;The decrease is primarily due to the use of $1.6 million in cash for the repurchase of our common stock in fiscal 2014. Net trade receivables were $1.2 million and $1.3 million at January 31, 2014 and 2013, respectively.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3425><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3426><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;Our total assets increased from $13.9 million at January 31, 2013 to $14.1&nbsp;million at January 31, 2014. Stockholders&#8217; equity decreased approximately 7.3% from&nbsp;$13.1 million&nbsp;at January 31, 2013 to $12.1 million at January 31, 2014. This decrease in stockholders&#39; equity is primarily attributable to our stock buyback in fiscal 2014 in the amount of $1.6 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;The ratio of current assets to current liabilities was 8.5 to1 compared to 24.8 to 1 last year, primarily due to the increase in broker payable of $1.4 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3427><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3428><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our operating activities in fiscal 2014 provided $3.4 million in cash, compared to $0.3 million used in operating activities in fiscal 2013. Our financing activities included primarily $1.6 million used for the repurchase of our common stock in fiscal year 2014, compared to $1.8 million used in fiscal 2013.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3429><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3431><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B>Item&nbsp;7A.&nbsp;&nbsp;Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk</B></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3443><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B>Item&nbsp;9A.&nbsp;&nbsp;Controls and Procedures</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3444><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3445><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B>Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3446><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3447><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of the end of the period covered by this Annual Report on Form 10-K, we carried out an evaluation under the supervision and with the participation of our management, including the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, of the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures pursuant to Exchange Act Rule&nbsp;13a-15(b).&nbsp;&nbsp;Disclosure controls and procedures are controls and other procedures that are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in our reports filed under the Exchange Act, such as this Annual Report on Form 10-K, is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified by the SEC.&nbsp;&nbsp;Disclosure controls and procedures are also designed to ensure that such information is accumulated and communicated to our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, as appropriate, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3448><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" id=PARA6395.1><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<DIV style="WIDTH: 100%; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" id=PGBK6395 >
<DIV style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%" id=PGFTR6395 >&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" id=PGNUM6395 >14</DIV>

<DIV style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; WIDTH: 100%" id=PGHDR6395 >&nbsp;</DIV></DIV>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" id=PARA6395.2><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3449><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The evaluation of our disclosure controls and procedures included a review of their objectives and design, our implementation of them and their effect on the information generated for use in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the course of the controls evaluation, we reviewed any data errors or control problems that we had identified and sought to confirm that appropriate corrective actions, including process improvements, were being undertaken.&nbsp;&nbsp;This type of evaluation is performed on a quarterly basis so that the conclusions of management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, concerning the effectiveness of the disclosure controls can be reported in our periodic reports on Form 10-K and Form 10-Q.&nbsp;&nbsp; The overall goals of these various evaluation activities are to monitor our disclosure controls and procedures and to modify them as necessary.&nbsp;&nbsp;We intend to maintain the disclosure controls and procedures as dynamic systems that we adjust as circumstances merit.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3450><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3451><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Based on the results of our evaluation, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer have concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of January&nbsp;31, 2014.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3452><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3453><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B>Management&#8217;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3454><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3455><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting, as such term is defined in Exchange Act Rule&nbsp;13a-15(f).&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the supervision and with the participation of our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, we conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of January&nbsp;31, 2014 based on the guidelines established in<I> Internal Control&#8212;Integrated Framework</I> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO).&nbsp;&nbsp;Our internal control over financial reporting includes policies and procedures designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external reporting purposes in accordance with United States generally accepted accounting principles.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3456><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3457><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Based on the results of our evaluation, our management concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was effective, as described above, as of January&nbsp;31, 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have reviewed the results of management&#8217;s assessment with our Audit Committee.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3458><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3459><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B>Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3460><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3461><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">There were no changes in our internal control over financial reporting identified in connection with the evaluation required by paragraph (d)&nbsp;of Exchange Act Rule&nbsp;13a-15 that was conducted during the fiscal quarter ended January&nbsp;31, 2014 that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3462><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3463><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;<B>Management Certifications</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3464><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3465><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The certifications of our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer required in accordance with Section&nbsp;302 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002, as amended,&nbsp;are attached as an exhibit to this Annual Report on Form 10-K.&nbsp;&nbsp;The disclosures set forth in this Item&nbsp;9A contain information concerning (i)&nbsp;the evaluation of our disclosure controls and procedures referred to in paragraph 4 of the certifications and (ii)&nbsp;material weaknesses in the operation of our internal control over financial reporting referred to in paragraph 5 of the certifications.&nbsp;&nbsp;Those certifications should be read in conjunction with this Item&nbsp;9A for a more complete understanding of the matters covered by the certifications.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3466><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3467><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B>Inherent Limitations on Effectiveness of Controls</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3468><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3469><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our management, comprised of our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, does not expect that our disclosure controls and procedures or our internal control over financial reporting will prevent all errors and all frauds.&nbsp;&nbsp;A control system, no matter how well conceived and operated, can provide only reasonable, not absolute, assurance that the objectives of the control system are met.&nbsp;&nbsp;Further, the design of a control system must reflect the fact that there are resource constraints, and the benefits of controls must be considered relative to their costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Because of the inherent limitations in all control systems, no evaluation of controls can provide absolute assurance that all control issues and instances of fraud, if any, within a company have been detected.&nbsp;&nbsp;These inherent limitations include the realities that judgments in decision making can be faulty, and that breakdowns can occur because of a simple error or mistake.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, controls can be circumvented by the individual acts of some persons, by collusion of two or more people or by management override of the controls.&nbsp;&nbsp;The design of any system of controls also is based in part upon certain assumptions about the likelihood of future events, and there can be no assurance that any design will succeed in achieving its stated goals under all potential future conditions; over time, controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or the degree of compliance with policies or procedures may deteriorate.&nbsp;&nbsp;Because of the inherent limitations in a cost-effective control system, misstatements due to error or fraud may occur and not be detected.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3470><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3471><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B>Item&nbsp;9B.&nbsp;&nbsp;Other Information</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3472><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3473><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Not applicable.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"></FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3867><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B>Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3868><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3869><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Board of Directors and Stockholders of Peerless Systems Corporation</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3870><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3871><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Peerless Systems Corporation as of January&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, and the related consolidated statements of operations, comprehensive loss, stockholders&#8217; equity, and cash flows for the years then ended.&nbsp;&nbsp;These consolidated financial statements are the responsibility of the Company&#8217;s management.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these consolidated financial statements based on our audits. </FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3872><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3873><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the consolidated financial statements are free of material misstatement. The Company is not required to have, nor were we engaged to perform, an audit of its internal control over financial reporting. Our audits included consideration of internal control over financial reporting as a basis for designing audit procedures that are appropriate in the circumstances, but not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting. &nbsp;Accordingly we express no such opinion. &nbsp;An audit also includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the consolidated financial statements, assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall consolidated financial statement presentation. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3874><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3875><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements referred to above present fairly, in all material respects, the consolidated financial position of Peerless Systems Corporation as of January&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, and the consolidated results of its operations and its cash flows for the years then ended, in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" id=PARA3964.2><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3965><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3966><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B>PEERLESS SYSTEMS CORPORATION</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3967><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3968><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3969><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3970><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B>1.&nbsp;&nbsp; Organization, Business and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies:</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3971><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3972><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;<I>Organization and Business:</I> Peerless Systems Corporation (&#8220;Peerless&#8221; or the &#8220;Company&#8221;) was incorporated in the state of California in April&nbsp;1982 and reincorporated in the state of Delaware in September&nbsp;1996.&nbsp;&nbsp;Peerless develops and licenses software-based digital imaging and networking systems and supporting electronic technologies to original equipment manufacturers (&#8220;OEMs&#8221;) of digital document products located primarily in the United States and Japan.&nbsp;&nbsp;Digital document products include printers, copiers, fax machines, scanners and color products, as well as multifunction products (&#8220;MFPs&#8221;) that perform a combination of these imaging functions.&nbsp;&nbsp;In order to process digital text and graphics, digital document products rely on a core set of imaging software and supporting electronics, collectively known as a digital imaging system.&nbsp;&nbsp;Network interfaces supply the core technologies to digital document products that enable them to communicate over local area networks and the Internet.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3973><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3974><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On April 30, 2008, the Company sold substantially all of its assets to Kyocera-Mita Corporation (&#8220;KMC&#8221;).&nbsp;&nbsp;In this transaction (the &#8220;KMC Transaction&#8221;), the Company retained certain intellectual property and also entered into a license agreement with KMC whereby it has the right to sublicense the technology to third parties. Following the completion of the KMC Transaction, the Company continues to license and market its remaining technology and the technology licensed from KMC directly to customers.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3975><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3976><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Since the closing of the KMC Transaction, the Company has reduced its focus on its legacy business and is seeking to use its excess cash to pursue transactions that enhance stockholder value.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has been engaged in efforts to identify appropriate acquisition targets that offer prospects for growth and profitability at a reasonable price.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3977><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3978><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Liquidity:</I> As of January&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company had cumulative retained earnings of $5.8&nbsp;million; the Company also had cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities (net of broker payable of $1.4 million included in other current liabilities) of $10.9&nbsp;million and net working capital of $ 12.4&nbsp;million.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has no material financial commitments.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company believes that its existing cash and cash equivalents and any cash generated from operations will be sufficient to fund its working capital requirements, capital expenditures and other obligations through the next twelve months.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3979><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3980><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Principles of Consolidation and Basis of Presentation:</I> The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of the Company and its subsidiaries.&nbsp;&nbsp;All significant intercompany accounts and transactions have been eliminated.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3981><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3982><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Use of Estimates:</I> The preparation of financial statements in conformity with </FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (GAAP) requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the consolidated financial statements and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting periods.&nbsp;&nbsp;Actual results could differ from those estimates.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3983><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3984><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company provides an accrual for estimated product licensing costs owed to third party vendors whose technology is included in the products sold by the Company.&nbsp;&nbsp;The accrual is impacted by estimates of the mix of products shipped under certain of the Company&#8217;s block license agreements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The estimates are based on historical data and available information as provided by the Company&#8217;s customers concerning projected shipments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Should actual shipments under these agreements vary from these estimates, adjustments to the estimated accruals for product licensing costs may be required.&nbsp;&nbsp;Actual results have historically been consistent with management&#8217;s estimates.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3985><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3986><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company grants credit terms in the normal course of business to its customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company continuously monitors collections and payments from its customers and maintains an allowance for doubtful accounts for estimated losses resulting from the inability of any customers to make required payments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Estimated losses are based primarily on specifically identified customer collection issues.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the financial condition of any of the Company&#8217;s customers, or the economy as a whole, were to deteriorate, resulting in an impairment of their ability to make payments, additional allowances may be required.&nbsp;&nbsp;Actual results have historically been consistent with management&#8217;s estimates. The allowance for doubtful accounts carried a zero balance as of January 31, 2014 and 2013. </FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3987><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3988><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The recognition of the Company&#8217;s recurring product licensing revenues is dependent, in part, on the timing and accuracy of product sales reports received from the Company&#8217;s OEM customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;These reports are primarily provided only on a calendar quarter basis and, in any event, are subject to delay and potential revision by the OEM.&nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore, the Company is required to estimate all of the recurring product licensing revenues for the last month of each fiscal quarter and to further estimate all of its quarterly revenues from an OEM when the report from such OEM is not received in a timely manner.&nbsp;&nbsp;As such, the Company accrued licensing revenues of $417,000 and $467,000 for the fiscal years ended January 31, 2014 and 2013, respectively. In the event the Company is unable to estimate such revenues accurately prior to reporting financial results, the Company may be required to adjust revenues in subsequent periods.&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3989><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" id=PARA3182.1><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" id=PARA3182.2><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3991><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Cash and Cash Equivalents:</I> Cash and cash equivalents represent cash and highly liquid investments, which mature within three months of purchase.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I></I></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Fair Value of Financial Instruments:</I> Cash and cash equivalents, accounts receivable, accounts payable, and accrued liabilities are carried at cost, which management believes approximates fair value due to the short term maturity of these instruments. </FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The fair values described herein were determined using significant other observable inputs (Level 2), except for cash and cash equivalents which use quoted market prices (Level 1), as defined by GAAP</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3994><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3996><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Marketable Securities:</I> The Company makes investments of cash in liquid interest bearing accounts and marketable securities. Marketable securities, as of January 31, 2014,&nbsp;were classified as available-for-sale, in accordance with ASC 320, &#8220;Investments &#8211; Debt and Equity Securities&#8221;, and are stated at fair market value, with any unrealized gains or losses reported as other comprehensive income (loss) under shareholders&#8217; equity in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Realized gains or losses and declines in value that are other than temporary, if any, on available-for-sale securities are calculated using the average cost method and are reported in other income or expense as incurred.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3997><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 39.6pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3998><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During the year, the Company made investments in available-for-sale and trading securities, as defined by ASC 320.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company classified securities that were purchased or sold with the intent to dispose within a short period as trading securities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Trading securities generally consisted of exchanged-listed securities such as common stock and equity options.&nbsp;&nbsp;Available-for-sale securities generally consisted of exchanged-listed securities such as common stock. Realized gains or losses on trading and available-for-sale securities are recorded in the statement of operations in other income, net.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA3999><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4000><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Property and Equipment:</I> Property and equipment are stated at cost, less accumulated depreciation.&nbsp;&nbsp;Depreciation on property and equipment is calculated using the straight-line method as follows:</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4001><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
