<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4009><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4010><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Maintenance and repairs are expensed as incurred, while renewals and betterments are capitalized.&nbsp;&nbsp;Upon the sale or retirement of property and equipment, the accounts are relieved of the cost and the related accumulated depreciation, and any resulting gain or loss is included in results of operations.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4011><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4012><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Long-Lived Assets:</I> The Company currently evaluates long-lived assets, including intangible assets, for impairment when events or changes indicate, in management&#8217;s judgment, that the carrying value of such assets may not be recoverable.&nbsp;&nbsp;The determination of whether an impairment has occurred is based upon management&#8217;s estimate of undiscounted future cash flows attributable to the assets as compared to the carrying value of the assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;If an impairment has occurred, the amount of the impairment recognized is determined by estimating the fair value of the assets and recording a write-down to reduce the related asset to its estimated fair value.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4013><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4014><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Revenue Recognition:</I> The Company recognizes software revenues in accordance with FASB ASC 985-605 &#8220;Software Revenue Recognition.&#8221;&nbsp;&nbsp;For certain of the Company&#8217;s multiple element arrangements that do not directly involve licensing, selling, leasing or otherwise marketing of the Company&#8217;s software the Company applies the guidance ASC 605-25 &#8220;Multiple-Element Arrangements.&#8221;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4015><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; MARGIN: 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Development license revenues from the licensing of source code or software development kits (&#8220;SDKs&#8221;) for the Company&#8217;s standard products are recognized upon delivery to and acceptance by the customer of the software if no significant modification or customization of the software is required and collection of the resulting receivable is probable.&nbsp;&nbsp;If modification or customization is essential to the functionality of the software, the development license revenues are recognized over the course of the modification work.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4017><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4018><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company has been party to engineering services contracts with certain OEMs&nbsp;adapting&nbsp;software and supporting electronics to specific OEM requirements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company provided engineering support based on a time-and-material basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenue from this support was recognized as the services were performed.&nbsp;The Company has allowed service and maintenance contracts with customers to expire and has decided not to renew such contracts.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4019><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4020><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Recurring licensing revenues are derived from per unit fees paid by the Company&#8217;s customers upon manufacturing and subsequent commercial shipment of products incorporating Peerless technology and certain third party technology, of which the Company is a sub-licensor.&nbsp;&nbsp;These recurring licensing revenues are recognized on a per unit basis as products are shipped commercially.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company sells block licenses, that is, specific quantities of licensed units that may be shipped in the future, or the Company may require the customer to pay minimum royalty commitments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Associated payments are typically made in one lump sum or extend over a period of four or more quarters.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company generally recognizes revenues associated with block licenses and minimum royalty commitments on delivery and acceptance of software, when collection of the resulting receivable is probable, when the fee is fixed and determinable, and when the Company has no significant future obligations.&nbsp;&nbsp;In cases where block licenses or minimum royalty commitments have extended payment terms and the fees are not fixed and determinable, revenue is recognized as payments become due.&nbsp;&nbsp;Further, when earned royalties exceed minimum royalty commitments, revenues are recognized on a per unit basis as products are shipped commercially.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4021><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" id=PARA3918.1><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<DIV style="WIDTH: 100%; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" id=PGBK3918 >
<DIV style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%" id=PGFTR3918 >F-9&nbsp;</DIV>
<DIV style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" id=PGNUM3918 >&nbsp;</DIV>
<HR style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%; HEIGHT: 2px; COLOR: #000000" noShade>

<DIV style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; WIDTH: 100%" id=PGHDR3918 >&nbsp;</DIV></DIV>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" id=PARA3918.2><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4022><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Perpetual licensing revenues are derived from fees paid by the Company&#8217;s customers to use the software indefinitely.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company generally recognizes revenues associated with perpetual licenses on delivery and acceptance of software, when collection of the resulting receivable is probable, when the fee is fixed and determinable, and when the Company has no significant future obligations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Associated payments are typically made in one lump sum.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4023><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4024><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For fees on multiple element software arrangements, values are allocated among the elements based on vendor specific objective evidence of fair value (&#8220;VSOE&#8221;).&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company generally establishes VSOE based upon the price charged when the same elements are sold separately.&nbsp;&nbsp;When VSOE exists for all undelivered elements, but not for the delivered elements, revenue is recognized using the &#8220;residual method.&#8221;&nbsp;&nbsp;If VSOE does not exist for the undelivered elements, all revenue for the arrangement is deferred until the earlier of the point at which such VSOE does exist for the undelivered elements or all elements of the arrangement have been delivered, unless the only undelivered element is a service in which revenue from the delivered element is recognized over the service period.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4025><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4026><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Deferred revenue consists of prepayments of licensing fees, payments billed to customers in advance of revenue recognized on engineering services or support contracts, and shipments of controllers that have not been sold to end users.&nbsp;&nbsp;Unbilled receivables arise when the revenue recognized on engineering support or block license contracts exceeds billings due to timing differences related to billing milestones as specified in the contract.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4027><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4028><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Income Taxes:</I> Deferred income taxes are recognized for the tax consequences in future years resulting from differences between the tax bases of assets and liabilities and their financial reporting amounts at each year-end based on enacted tax laws and statutory rates applicable to the periods in which the differences are expected to reverse.&nbsp;&nbsp;Valuation allowances are established, when necessary, to reduce deferred income tax assets to the amount expected to be realized.&nbsp;&nbsp;Income tax provision is the tax payable for the period and the change during the period in net deferred income tax assets and liabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;See Note 5.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4029><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4030><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Comprehensive Income:</I> In accordance with ASC 220, &#8220;Comprehensive Income,&#8221; all components of comprehensive income, including net income, are reported in the consolidated financial statements in the period in which they are recognized.&nbsp;&nbsp;Other comprehensive income includes unrealized gains and losses on available-for-sale securities. Comprehensive income is defined as the change in equity during a period from transactions and other events and circumstances from non-owner sources.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#8217;s accumulated other comprehensive loss for fiscal years ended January&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013 consisted of net income and unrealized gains or losses and is reported in stockholders&#8217; equity.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4031><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4032><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Earnings Per Share:</I> Basic earnings per share (&#8220;basic EPS&#8221;) is computed by dividing net income available to common stockholders (the numerator) by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding (the denominator) during the period.&nbsp;&nbsp;The computation of diluted earnings per share (&#8220;diluted EPS&#8221;) is similar to the computation of basic EPS except that the denominator is increased to include the number of additional common shares that would have been outstanding if dilutive potential common shares had been issued.&nbsp;&nbsp;Potential common shares include outstanding options under the Company&#8217;s employee stock option plan and incrementally vested service-vesting restricted stock awards (which are included under the treasury stock method).&nbsp;&nbsp;A reconciliation of basic EPS to diluted EPS is presented in Note 6 to the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4033><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4034><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Foreign Currency Translation:</I> The financial statements of the Company&#8217;s former non-U.S. subsidiary are translated into U.S. dollars in accordance with ASC 830, &#8220;Foreign Currency Matters.&#8221; The assets and liabilities of the Company&#8217;s non-U.S. subsidiary whose &#8220;functional&#8221; currency is other than the U.S. dollar are translated at current rates of exchange.&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenue and expense items are translated at the average exchange rate for the year.&nbsp;&nbsp;The resulting translated adjustments are recorded directly into accumulated other comprehensive income.&nbsp;&nbsp;Transaction gains and losses are included in net income in the period they occur.&nbsp;&nbsp;Foreign currency translation and transaction gains and losses have not been significant in any period presented.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4035><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 31.9pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4036><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Recent Accounting Pronouncements:</I></FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;In February 2013, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) issued Accounting Standards Update (&#8220;ASU&#8221;) No. 2013-02, &#8220;Reporting Amounts Reclassified Out of Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income,&#8221; which amends Accounting Standards Codification (&#8220;ASC&#8221;) 220, &#8220;Comprehensive Income.&#8221; The amended guidance requires entities to provide information about the amounts reclassified out of accumulated other comprehensive income by component. Additionally, entities are required to present, either on the face of the financial statements or in the notes, significant amounts reclassified out of accumulated other comprehensive income by the respective line items of net income. The amended guidance does not change the current requirements for reporting net income or other comprehensive income. The amendment is effective prospectively for annual periods, and interim periods within those annual periods, beginning after December 15, 2012. The new guidance did not have a material impact on the Company&#8217;s financial statements for each year ended January&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4037><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4039><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4040><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B>2.&nbsp;&nbsp; Cash, Cash Equivalents and Marketable Securities</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4041><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4042><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On February&nbsp;1, 2008, the Company adopted the provisions of FASB ASC Topic 820, Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures (formerly known as FAS 157 Fair Value Measurements), which clarifies that fair value is an exit price, representing the amount that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants.&nbsp;&nbsp;As such, fair value is a market-based measurement that should be determined based on assumptions that market participants would use in pricing an asset or liability.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a basis for considering such assumptions, Topic 820 establishes a three-tier value hierarchy, which prioritizes the inputs used in measuring fair value as follows: (Level I) observable inputs such as quoted prices in active markets; (Level II) inputs other than the quoted prices in active markets that are observable either directly or indirectly; and (Level III) unobservable inputs in which there is little or no market data, which requires the Company to develop its own assumptions.&nbsp;&nbsp;This hierarchy requires the Company to use observable market data, when available, and to minimize the use of unobservable inputs when determining fair value.&nbsp;&nbsp;On a recurring basis, the Company measures its marketable securities at fair value.&nbsp;&nbsp;Marketable securities are classified within Level I of the fair value hierarchy because they are valued using quoted market prices.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4043><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4044><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of January 31, 2014 and 2013, cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities included the following (in thousands):</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4051><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4052><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;<B>3. Stock-Based Compensation Plans</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4053><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4054><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company has certain plans which provide for the grant of incentive stock options to employees and non-statutory stock options, restricted stock purchase awards and stock bonuses to employees, directors and consultants.&nbsp;&nbsp;The terms of stock options granted under these plans generally may not exceed 10&nbsp;years.&nbsp;&nbsp;Options granted under these plans vest at the rate specified in each optionee&#8217;s agreement, generally over three or four years</FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Since July 1996, an aggregate of 5.2&nbsp;million shares of common stock have been authorized for issuance under the various option plans. </FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4055><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4057><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>1996 Incentive Plan:</I> In May&nbsp;1996, the Board of Directors adopted the Company&#8217;s 1996 Stock Option Plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#8217;s 1996 Equity Incentive Plan (the &#8220;1996 Incentive Plan&#8221;) was adopted by the Board of Directors in July&nbsp;1996 as an amendment and restatement of the Company&#8217;s 1996 Plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;At that time, the Board of Directors had authorized and reserved an aggregate of 1,267,000 shares of common stock for issuance under the 1996 Incentive Plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additional shares&nbsp;of common stock were authorized and reserved for issuance under the 1996 Incentive Plan in June&nbsp;1998, June&nbsp;1999, June 2001, and June&nbsp;2003 in the amounts of 1,200,000, 750,000, 750,000, and 700,000 shares, respectively.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4058><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" id=PARA3422.1><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" id=PARA3422.2><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4059><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>2005 Incentive Stock Option Plan:</I> In June&nbsp;2005, stockholders approved the Company&#8217;s 2005 Equity Incentive Plan (the &#8220;2005 Incentive Plan&#8221;).&nbsp;&nbsp;The Board authorized and reserved 500,000 shares together with the 289,000 shares remaining under the 1996 Incentive Plan which was terminated as authorized by the stockholders. As of January 31, 2014, there are approximately 267,000 shares available for future grants.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4060><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4061><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The 2005 Incentive Plan&nbsp;allows for the grant of incentive stock options to employees and non-statutory stock options, restricted stock purchase awards and stock bonuses to employees, directors and consultants.&nbsp;&nbsp;The terms of stock options granted under the 2005 Incentive Plan generally may not exceed 10&nbsp;years.&nbsp;&nbsp;The exercise price of options granted under the 2005 Incentive Plan is determined by the Board of Directors, provided that the exercise price for an incentive stock option cannot be less than 100% of the fair market value of the common stock on the date of the option grant and the exercise price for a non-statutory stock option cannot be less than 85% of the fair market value of the common stock on the date of the option grant.&nbsp;&nbsp;Options granted under the 2005 Incentive Plan vest at the rate specified in each optionee&#8217;s agreement, which is generally over 3 to 4&nbsp;years.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4062><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4063><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following represents option activity under the 1996 Incentive Plan and 2005 Incentive Plan for the fiscal years ended January&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013:</FONT></P>

<TD style="PADDING-BOTTOM: 3px; BACKGROUND-COLOR: #ffffff; WIDTH: 1%; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" id=TBL3486.finRow.12.trail.5 noWrap>&nbsp;</TD></TR></TABLE>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4066><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4067><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The weighted-average fair value as of date of grant of the options granted during the years ended January&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013 were $1.47 and $1.90, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;During the years ended January&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, the total intrinsic value of stock options exercised was $8,700 and $205,341, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;Cash received from stock option exercises in fiscal 2014 and fiscal 2013 was $41,550 and $4,390, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the Company also received 26,389 company shares valued at $99,750 in connection with a stock option exercised in fiscal 2013, which was accounted for as treasury stock.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4068><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4069><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The valuation methodologies and assumptions in estimating the fair value of stock options that were granted in fiscal 2014 were similar to those used in estimating the fair value of stock options granted in fiscal 2013 by using the Black-Scholes model.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company uses historical volatility of Peerless&#8217; stock price as a basis to determine the expected volatility assumption to value stock options.&nbsp;&nbsp;The expected volatility was calculated based upon the changes in the price of the Company&#8217;s common stock over a five year period. </FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;The expected dividend yield is based on Peerless&#8217; practice of not paying dividends.&nbsp;&nbsp;The risk-free rate of return is based on the yield of a U.S. Treasury instrument with terms approximating or equal to the expected term of the option.&nbsp;&nbsp;The expected life in years is based on historical actual stock option exercise experience. During fiscal 2014, the Company used the weighted average expected lives of 7.0&nbsp;years, expected volatility of 36.3%, and weighted average risk free interest rate of 1.23%.&nbsp;&nbsp;During fiscal 2013, the Company used the weighted average expected lives of 7.8&nbsp;years, expected volatility of 42.5%, and weighted average risk free interest rate of 1.75%.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4070><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4071><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Compensation expenses for share-based awards granted are recognized using a straight-line, or single-option method.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company recognizes these compensation costs over the service period of the award, which is generally the option vesting term of three or four years.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In fiscal 2014 and 2013, the Company recorded a total of $96,000 and $139,000, respectively, in stock option expense related to stock options awarded.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4072><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4073><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The excess tax benefit from exercised options was approximately $8,700 for the year ended January&nbsp;31, 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of January&nbsp;31, 2014, there was $42,572 of total unrecognized compensation cost related to non-vested share-based compensation arrangements granted under the 1996 and 2005 Incentive Plans and certain options issued outside these plans.&nbsp;&nbsp;That cost is expected to be recognized over a weighted-average period of 1.99&nbsp;years.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company issues shares of common stock reserved for such plans upon the exercise of stock options.&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4074><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" id=PARA3615.2><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4075><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During fiscal 2014, the Company granted 258,088 shares of restricted stock to its directors and employees pursuant to the 2005 Incentive Plan, including approximately 250,000 shares related to the market-based award noted below.&nbsp;&nbsp;During fiscal 2014, 67,907 shares of restricted common stock vested with an aggregated fair market value at the vesting dates of $254,501</FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The related stock based compensation expense of approximately $865,000 has been recorded for the year ended January 31, 2014</FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">, including approximately $812,000 related to the market-based award noted below. </FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4076><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4077><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During fiscal 2013, the Company granted 17,577 shares of restricted stock to its directors and employees pursuant to the 2005 Incentive Plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;During fiscal 2013, 52,202 shares of restricted common stock vested with an aggregated fair market value at the vesting dates of $199,794.&nbsp;&nbsp;The related stock based compensation expense of approximately $102,000 has been recorded for the year ended January 31, 2013</FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">. </FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4078><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 50.6pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4079><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In connection with the new employment agreement entered into on July 11, 2013 with Mr. Timothy Brog, the Company&#8217;s Chairman and Chief Executive Officer (the &#8220;Employment Agreement&#8221;), Mr. Brog agreed to forfeit 150,000 shares of restricted common stock that remained unvested under the previous employment agreement between the Company and Mr. Brog dated August 26, 2010 (the &#8220;2010 Agreement&#8221;). As part of the Employment Agreement, the Company granted 250,000 shares of restricted common stock to Mr. Brog. Although the fair value of the newly granted restricted common stock would be amortized as stock-based compensation, there would be no offset from the fair value previously expensed relating to the 150,000 shares that were forfeited due to the fact that the requisite service period had been satisfied.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 39.6pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4080><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 39.6pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4081><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company used a Monte Carlo simulation model valuation technique to determine the fair value of the 250,000 restricted shares granted to Mr. Brog, because these awards vest based upon achievement of market price targets or a &#8220;market condition,&#8221; one quarter of which will vest if prior to July 11, 2017 the average closing price of the Company&#8217;s Common Stock on the Nasdaq Capital Market is greater than or equal to the target prices of $3.75, $4.00, $4.25 and $4.50, respectively, for 15 consecutive trading days. On the date of the grant, the closing price of the common stock was $3.76.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 39.6pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4082><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 39.6pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4083><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">All such shares will also vest in the event that the Company (i) announces its intent to terminate its registration of the Common Stock under Section 12(g) of the Securities and Exchange Act of 1934, (ii) commences a self-tender offer for not less than 33% of the outstanding Common Stock, at an offer price at least equal to the average closing price over the preceding 15 trading days, or (iii) completes any other extraordinary transaction in which shares of the Company equal to not less than 20% of the shares of outstanding Common Stock immediately prior to such transaction are issued as part of such transaction.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4084><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 39.6pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4085><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Monte Carlo simulation model utilizes multiple input variables that determine the probability of satisfying the market condition stipulated in the award and calculates the fair value of each share of the restricted stock. The Company used the following assumptions in determining the fair value of the awards granted on July 11, 2013:</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4106><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The daily expected stock price volatility is based on four-year historical volatility of the Company&#8217;s common stock. The daily expected dividend yield is based on annual expected dividend payments and the closing price of the Company&#8217;s common stock on the Nasdaq Capital Market on the date of the grant. The average daily risk-free interest rate is based on the three-year treasury yield as of the grant date. Each of the four tranches of the restricted stock grant is calculated to have its own fair value and requisite service period. The fair value of each tranche is amortized over the lesser of the requisite or derived service period which is up to four years. These shares had an aggregate grant date fair value of $812,000. This award was fully expensed as of January 31, 2014. As of January 31, 2014, 62,500 shares were vested under this grant with a fair market value of $235,000.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4139><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The effective tax rate for fiscal 2014 was lower than the statutory rate because of a $157,000 increase in valuation allowance related to certain stock-based compensation recorded during the year, net of certain restricted stock that vested during the same period. The effective tax rate for fiscal 2013 was lower than the statutory rate because of a reversal of $1,265,000 in tax liabilities related to an unrecognized tax benefit from the Company&#8217;s tax position taken for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2009, in connection with the completion of the three year statute of limitations period applicable to the corresponding tax return, as discussed below.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 29.7pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4140><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4141><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On February&nbsp;1, 2007, the Company adopted ASC 740-10.&nbsp;&nbsp;ASC 740-10 clarifies the accounting and reporting for uncertainties in income tax law.&nbsp;&nbsp;This Interpretation prescribes a comprehensive model for the financial statement recognition, measurement, presentation and disclosure of uncertain tax positions taken or expected to be taken in income tax returns.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Interpretation requires that the tax effects of a position be recognized only if it is &#8220;more-likely-than-not&#8221; to be sustained by the taxing authority as of the reporting date.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the tax position is not considered &#8220;more-likely-than-not&#8221; to be sustained, then no benefits of the position are to be recognized.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4142><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4143><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">There was no cumulative effect of adopting ASC 740-10 to the February&nbsp;1, 2007 retained earnings balance.&nbsp;&nbsp;On the date of adoption, the Company had $2.0&nbsp;million of unrecognized tax benefits, all of which would reduce its effective tax rate if recognized.&nbsp;&nbsp;A reconciliation of the beginning and ending amount of unrecognized tax benefits for fiscal years 2014 and 2013 is as follows:</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4161><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Potentially dilutive options in the aggregate of approximately 122,000 and 145,000 in fiscal years 2014 and 2013, respectively, have been excluded from the calculation of the diluted income per share based on (i) the fact that the exercise prices of such options exceeds the average stock price and (ii) the number of buy back shares exceeded the assumed shares issued upon exercise of options.&nbsp;&nbsp;For these reasons, these options were considered anti-dilutive. In addition, dilutive options of approximately 129,000 in fiscal 2014 have been excluded from the calculation of the diluted loss per share because it would otherwise result in a reduction in loss per share.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4163><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;<B>7</B>. <B>Common Stock Repurchases:</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4164><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 29.7pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4165><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During the fiscal year ended January 31, 2014, the Company repurchased 450,091 shares of its common stock for an aggregate purchase price of $1,620,458.&nbsp;&nbsp; From February 1, 2014 through April 17, 2014, the Company repurchased an additional 19,903 shares of its common stock for an aggregate purchase price of $74,095.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 29.7pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4166><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4167><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;<B>8.&nbsp;&nbsp;Employee Savings Plan:</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4168><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4169><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company maintains an employee savings plan that qualifies under Section 401(k) of the Internal Revenue Code (the &#8220;Code&#8221;) for its full-time employees.&nbsp;&nbsp;The plan allows employees to make specified percentage pretax contributions up to the maximum dollar limitation prescribed by the Code.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company matches 50% of employee contributions up to a maximum of $2,000 per employee per year. Company contributions to the plan during the years ended January&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013 were $4,300 and $5,300, respectively.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4170><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4171><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B>9.&nbsp;&nbsp;Segment Reporting:</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4172><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4173><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company operates in one reportable business segment, Imaging.&nbsp;&nbsp;Peerless provides software-based digital imaging and networking technology for digital document products and provides directory and management software for networked storage devices and integrates proprietary software into enterprise networks of OEMs. </FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4174><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4175><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A limited number of these OEM customers continue to provide a substantial portion of our revenues in fiscal 2014 and fiscal 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;T</FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">here were three OEM customers, Novell, KMC and Oki Data</FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">, each of which constituted customers representing 10% or more of our total revenues in fiscal 2014 and/or fiscal 2013, and collectively accounted for 93% and 70% of our revenues for fiscal 2014 and fiscal 2013, respectively. </FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4176><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4193><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4194><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During fiscal year 2014, the Company reported approximately $2,208,000 of other loss, representing primarily $2,217,000 of realized loss on marketable securities. </FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4195><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 49.5pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4196><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During fiscal year 2013, the Company reported approximately $173,000 of other income, representing primarily $111,000 of reversal of accrued interest expenses related to tax liabilities and $58,000 of realized gains on marketable securities.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4197><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4198><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B>12.&nbsp;&nbsp;Risks and Uncertainties:</B></FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4199><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4200><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Concentration of Credit Risk:</I> The Company&#8217;s credit risk in accounts receivable (trade and unbilled), which are generally not collateralized, is concentrated with customers which are OEMs of laser printers and printer peripheral technologies.&nbsp;&nbsp;The financial loss, should a customer be unable to meet its obligation to the Company, would be equal to the recorded accounts receivable.&nbsp;&nbsp;At January&nbsp;31, 2014, three customers collectively represented approximately 93% of total accounts receivable and three customers collectively represented approximately 90% at January&nbsp;31, 2013.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4201><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4202><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A significant portion of the Company&#8217;s revenue is generated from recurring quarterly shipments made by its OEM customers</FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the past, block licenses and perpetual licenses contributed to more of the Company&#8217;s revenue. Recurring revenue from quarterly shipments represented 100% in fiscal 2014 and fiscal 2013 because there were no block licenses or perpetual licenses sold during that two year period. Revenue from recurring quarterly shipments from our customers exposes us to more credit risk as payments are made on a quarterly basis, rather than with block licenses which are paid in advance.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4203><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4204><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Litigation:</I> The Company is involved from time to time in various claims and legal actions incident to its operations, either as plaintiff or defendant.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the opinion of management, after consulting with legal counsel, no claims are currently expected to have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s financial position, operating results, or cash flows.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4205><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4206><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>License Agreements:&nbsp;&nbsp;</I>The Company&#39;s&nbsp;historical business has consisted of (i) products with Peerless developed intellectual property, (ii) products based upon an agreement with Novell (&#8220;Novell&#8221;) and (iii) products based upon an agreement with Adobe Systems Corporation&nbsp;(&#8220;Adobe&#8221;) to bundle and sublicense Adobe&#8217;s licensed products into products for OEMs. The Company&#8217;s agreement with Adobe to bundle and sublicense Adobe&#8217;s licensed products into new OEM products expired on March 31, 2010.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is&nbsp;unlikely to be able to transition its customer base to another provider which will have an impact on Adobe related licensing revenues for the coming years. Our revenues from licensing products that include Adobe technology were approximately $0.8 million and $0.7 million for fiscal 2014 and 2013, respectively.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; LINE-HEIGHT: 1.25; TEXT-INDENT: 44pt; MARGIN: 0pt" id=PARA4207><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
